wordList.title: Air steps ("Aerials", "Akro")
wordList.description: Terminology: "Flyer": the person flying through the air (often the follower), "Thrower": the person staying on the ground (often the leader). Where possible we use the original names of the steps.

words.description: Starting from back charleston, the thrower lifts the flyer up by their hands. Other names include: Kick through, Russian kick
Something like the shape of a swingout, but where the flyer flies around the thrower's back. Other names include: Lindy flip, Lamppost, Frankie flip
The thrower stands up straight, holding the flyer upside-down above them. Ideally they form a single vertical line
The flyer starts facing the thrower, who lifts them up and over the thrower's head, landing facing away from each other. Previously also known as a "Coochie toss"
The flyer does a full vertical spin centered on the thrower's right side. In some variations, the flyer ends by touching the ground with their hand. Named for Kay Smith

The first ever air step! Starting back to back, thrower and flyer link arms, and the thrower leans forward, sending the flyer over to land face to face. Other names include: Back to Back, Rygg kast (sv)
The flyer does a front flip facing the thrower and lands (staying in front of the thrower) with their arms around the thrower's neck

sometimes "Soptunnan" in Sweden. Flyer braces off the thrower's legs and goes over the thrower's shoulder, landing back-to-back. Not to be confused with "Over the shoulder" aka "Basket toss" where the flyer starts with their back to the thrower,
the thrower (usually the follower) holds their partner upside down, legs shaking in the air
we'll count any flip where the flyer goes backwards over the thrower's arm. Other names include: Hourglass, Baby Flip, Basket toss
any air step where the flyer dives down the thrower's back and ends up between their legs
